## 2026-08-26 - [Stored XSS Vulnerabilities in `popup.js`]
**Vulnerability:** In `popup.js`, dynamically generated DOM structures via `innerHTML` interpolated un-escaped variables retrieved from `chrome.storage.local` (e.g., `log.timestamp`, `log.type`, `srcLangText`, `timeText`, `item.id`). Although some variables like `log.message` and `item.srcText` were properly escaped, others were missed, leaving the extension vulnerable to Stored XSS.
**Learning:** Data from local storage, such as extension history or logs, should be treated as untrusted data, even if it is generated by the application itself. Any data retrieved from storage must be fully sanitized before being injected into the DOM.
**Prevention:** Always wrap dynamically interpolated variables in `escapeHTML()` when constructing `innerHTML` templates, particularly for values fetched from `chrome.storage.local`.
